title: AJ’s Anomaly
intro: AJ’s Anomaly is a short, single player, spot-the-difference horror game for Steam, built in Unreal Engine 5. Developed with one other person, this game features interactive puzzles, jump scares, and narrative sequences that tell the story of a fashion designer overcoming her trauma through anomaly therapy.

sections.heading: RAPID PROTOTYPING AND FINDING THE FUN
paragraphs: I spent a short time ramping up in Unreal Blueprints before switching to prototyping gameplay exclusively in C++, without AI-tooling.  Programming gameplay is a first for me but I took a course and was able to acclimate quickly and have been programming full-time since. I created about a dozen gameplay prototypes in first- and third-person, with systems like combat, AI-driven enemies, pickups, interactive maps, dialog, cinematics, data structures, and more before locking down the core feature set that we would move forward into production.

sections.heading: POLISHING AND FEEDBACK LOOPS
paragraphs: With the gameplay loop and content pipelines in place, we shifted some focus to polishing the UX/UI, character fidelity, and adding meta gameplay to facilitate a deeper narrative and build out a more complete player experience. Valuable feedback from early testers helped shape the pacing and narrative structure seen in the final version.

sections.heading: CO-DEVELOPING GAMES ON A TEAM OF 2
paragraphs: My colleague and I divided development roles and responsibilities nearly evenly.  I am responsible for gameplay programming, game design, and UI, and he is responsible for characters, sound, and narrative elements. We worked from a shared Git repo, tasked ourselves in Trello for visibility, and met on a regular basis to discuss priorities, discoveries, and more.  We built this game remotely in about 3 months.
